away.name: Joseph Woll
away.news: Joseph Woll has clearly outplayed Dan Vladar as the 2026-27 season begins and could earn more playing time if he keeps impressing. The 28-year-old Woll has saved 78 of 84 shots (.929 SV%) in two games this season, going 0-0-2 for a Flyers team that has been offensively miserable, scoring only five combined goals in four games (0-2-2). The Flyers enter Thursday's contest as +155 road underdogs against a 2-1-0 Ottawa Senators team.

home.name: Linus Ullmark
home.news: Ottawa's previous game raised concerns when Ullmark exited in the second intermission with an undisclosed injury. Still, he fully participated in the team's morning skate on Thursday and will return to the crease against the Philadelphia Flyers. The 33-year-old Swedish goalie had an up-and-down 2025-26 season, but has started 2026-27 on a positive note, with an impressive 1.20 GAA and .949 SV% in two outings (2-0-0). The Senators enter Thursday's contest as -175 home favourites against a Flyers team that has been outscored 17-5 through four games (0-2-2).

away.name: Alex Nedeljkovic
away.news: Sharks Head Coach Ryan Warsofsky rolled with Yaroslav Askarov for the first three games of the season (2-1-0), but Askarov hasn't provided confidence between the pipes, so Warsofsky will turn to Nedeljkovic for the first time on Thursday. The 30-year-old Nedeljkovic was a serviceable option when Askarov struggled last season, posting a 2.87 GAA and .896 SV% in 40 games (18-14-4). The Sharks enter Thursday's contest as +137 road underdogs against a St. Louis Blues team on a two-game losing streak (0-2-0).

home.name: Joel Hofer
home.news: To start the 2026-27 season, the Blues have made it clear they are relying more on Hofer than veteran Jordan Binnington, and will turn to him again on Thursday for his third start in four games. Through two games this season (1-1-0), Hofer has a shutout and has posted an impressive 1.01 GAA and .955 SV%. The Blues enter Thursday as -150 home favourites against a San Jose Sharks team coming off a disappointing 5-0 loss to the Dallas Stars.

away.name: Sebastian Cossa
away.news: Karel Vejmelka carried a heavy workload last season for Utah, and with rookie Sebastian Cossa as his backup for 2026-27, it was unclear how the crease would be split. That said, after a strong debut, saving 18 of 19 shots (.947 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets, the 23-year-old Cossa will return to the crease on Thursday for his second start in five games. The Mammoth enter Thursday as -121 road favourites against a Boston Bruins team that has scored only nine goals in four games (2-2-0).

home.name: Jeremy Swayman
home.news: Jeremy Swayman had a miserable 2024-25 season after signing a massive eight-year contract extension, posting an ugly 3.11 GAA and .892 SV% in 58 games (22-29-7). The organization had concerns about the contract, but he followed it up with a solid 2025-26 season, posting a 2.71 GAA and .907 SV% in 55 games (31-18-4). Now, the 27-year-old goalie seems to be continuing his upward trajectory, opening the season with a 2.30 GAA and .914 SV% in three games (2-1-0). That said, he is coming off his weakest performance of the season, allowing four goals on 24 shots (.833 SV%) in a 4-1 loss to the Ottawa Senators. Swayman hopes to rebound Thursday, as the Bruins enter as slight +112 home underdogs against the Utah Mammoth, who have outscored opponents 17-8 over four games (3-1-0).

away.name: Jake Oettinger
away.news: After a miserable start to the season, outscoring 6-1 in their first two games (0-2-0), the Stars are coming off a 5-0 statement win over the San Jose Sharks and hope to carry that momentum into Thursday's contest against the Buffalo Sabres. The 27-year-old Oettinger stopped all 13 shots for his first shutout of the season, improving to a 1.01 GAA and .943 SV% in two games (1-1-0). The Stars enter Thursday's contest as slight -114 road favourites against a 2-1-0 Buffalo Sabres team.

home.name: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen
home.news: Still without Alex Lyon (upper body), the Sabres will keep leaning on Luukkonen, turning to him for the third time in four games. That said, Luukkonen's de facto starting netminder role hasn't translated into success. The 27-year-old Finnish goalie has allowed eight goals on 37 shots (.784 SV%) in two outings, but has salvaged a 1-1-0 record. The Sabres enter Thursday's contest as slight +105 home underdogs against a Dallas Stars team coming off a one-sided 5-0 victory over the San Jose Sharks.

away.name: Juuse Saros
away.news: Saros has carried a heavy workload for the Predators in recent seasons, a trend that will continue into 2026-27, as he will tend the twine for the fourth straight time on Thursday. Despite Head Coach Andrew Brunette's trust, Saros is coming off his weakest outing of the season, allowing five goals on 37 shots (.865 SV%) in a 5-4 overtime loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. The 31-year-old Finnish goalie has a 2.95 GAA and .907 SV% through three games (1-1-1). The Predators enter Thursday's contest as +141 road underdogs against a Montreal Canadiens team that is 1-1-1 this season.

home.name: Jacob Fowler
home.news: Samuel Montembeault's disastrous 2025-26 season, which led to a demotion to the AHL, thrust Fowler into some NHL action, but Montembeault started the 2026-27 season with the Canadiens, resulting in Fowler playing with Laval (AHL). That said, an early-season injury to Montembeault has given Fowler an NHL opportunity, and he will tend the twine for the first time this season on Thursday against the Nashville Predators. The 21-year-old Fowler played well last season in his NHL debut, posting a 2.43 GAA and .908 SV% in 17 games (9-6-2). The Canadiens enter Thursday's contest as -171 home favourites.

away.name: Jesper Wallstedt
away.news: With Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined at the start of the season, Minnesota will continue to rely on Wallstedt, giving him his fourth straight start of 2026-27. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has given Head Coach John Hynes no reason to deviate, posting a stellar 1.63 GAA and .933 SV% in three games (2-0-1). Minnesota enters Thursday's contest as +127 road underdogs against a 2-1-0 Tampa Bay Lightning team.

home.name: Dennis Hildeby
home.news: Tampa Bay has relied heavily on Andrei Vasilevskiy in recent seasons, so its plan for 2026-27 with newcomer Dennis Hildeby remains unclear, but he will likely start on Thursday against the Minnesota Wild. The 25-year-old Hildeby benefited from team injuries last season as a member of the Toronto Maple Leafs, earning a promotion to the NHL, where he played well when called upon, posting a 2.86 GAA and .914 SV% in 20 appearances (5-7-4). Tampa Bay enters Thursday's contest as -139 home favourites against a Minnesota team that is 2-1-0 this season.

away.name: Kevin Lankinen
away.news: Vancouver's stoutest defensive outing of the season came with Leevi Merilainen between the pipes in a 4-1 win over the Calgary Flames. Still, the Canucks will turn to Lankinen on Thursday for his fourth start in five games. The 31-year-old Lankinen is coming off his best outing of the season, but he still struggled, allowing three goals on 28 shots (.893 SV%) in a 3-2 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. Lankinen has an ugly 6.50 GAA and .824 SV% in three games (1-2-0). The Canucks enter Thursday's contest as significant +290 road underdogs against a 2-1-1 Carolina Hurricanes team.

home.name: Pyotr Kochetkov
home.news: Hurricanes' Head Coach Rod Brind'Amour started Brandon Bussi in the first two games of the season, but he seems to be easing into an even goalie rotation, with Kochetkov tending the twine on Thursday in his second start of the season. The 27-year-old Kochetkov missed most of the 2025-26 season with a lower-body injury, but he played well in his return to action, saving 16 of 18 shots (.889 SV%) in a 3-2 win over the Philadelphia Flyers. The Hurricanes enter Thursday's contest as enormous -337 home favourites against the surprisingly potent early-season offense of the Vancouver Canucks, who have scored 19 goals in their first four games (2-2-0).

away.name: Arvid Soderblom
away.news: Soderblom will start vs. the Islanders on Thursday.

home.name: Ilya Sorokin
home.news: Sorokin had the night off in New York's previous game, but he will likely return to the crease on Thursday against the Chicago Blackhawks, looking to build on a strong start to the 2026-27 season. The 31-year-old goalie has been outstanding through two games, despite a 1-1-0 record, saving 61 of 63 combined shots (.968 SV%). Sorokin had the worst save percentage of his career in 2025-26 (.906 SV%) and hopes to improve those totals this season under new Head Coach Pete DeBoer.

away.name: Scott Wedgewood
away.news: Surprisingly, Colorado hasn't turned to Scott Wedgewood this season and has rolled with Blackwood between the pipes for the first three games. Wedgewood's tremendous 2025-26 season, posting a 2.02 GAA and .921 SV% in 45 appearances (31-6-6), should at least earn him close to a timeshare by season's end, even if the team is showing early-season favour for Blackwood. Colorado enters Thursday's contest as significant -235 road favourites against a struggling Calgary team that has been outscored 16-3 through three games (0-3-0).

home.name: Devin Cooley
home.news: Cooley had a terrific first season as a full-time NHLer, serving primarily as Dustin Wolf's backup, posting a solid 2.69 GAA and .909 SV% in 31 appearances (10-10-6) for a poor Calgary Flames team. The 29-year-old Cooley struggled in his only 2026-27 outing, allowing three goals on 25 shots (.880 SV%) in a 4-1 loss to the Vancouver Canucks, but hopes to improve Thursday against the Colorado Avalanche. The Flames enter Thursday's contest as sizeable +207 home underdogs against an Avalanche team coming off a disappointing final-minute 3-2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets yesterday.

home.name: Adin Hill
home.news: The Golden Knights have turned to Carter Hart in three of four games this season, but Hill played well in his only outing and will return to the crease on Thursday against the Toronto Maple Leafs. The 30-year-old Hill saved 18 of 20 shots in an October 4th 3-2 victory over the Vancouver Canucks. Hill is hoping to bounce back after an ugly 2025-26 season, posting a 3.04 GAA and .871 SV% in 27 appearances (10-9-6). The Golden Knights enter Thursday as -164 home favourites against a 2-2-0 Maple Leafs team.
